classification.difficultyReason: Independently turn standard quadrantal values into sketches on the specified half-turn interval, placing the sine maximum, cosine intercept and tangent asymptote and choosing the correct direction for each tangent branch.

content.prompt: Sketch the graphs of the following in the domain $x\in[0,\pi]$.

answer.short: A smooth sine arch through $(0,0)$, $(\frac{\pi}{2},1)$ and $(\pi,0)$.
answer.worked: Plot $(0,0)$, $(\frac{\pi}{2},1)$ and $(\pi,0)$. Join them with a smooth sine curve, rising to the maximum at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and returning to the horizontal axis at $x=\pi$.

spec.description: Sine arch on the requested half-turn interval.

answer.short: A smooth decreasing cosine curve through $(0,1)$, $(\frac{\pi}{2},0)$ and $(\pi,-1)$.
answer.worked: Plot $(0,1)$, $(\frac{\pi}{2},0)$ and $(\pi,-1)$. Join them with a smooth decreasing cosine curve.

spec.description: Decreasing cosine curve over the requested half-turn interval.

answer.short: Increasing branches with zeros at $x=0,\pi$ and vertical asymptote $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$.
answer.worked: Mark the zeros at $(0,0)$ and $(\pi,0)$ and draw the vertical asymptote $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$. On the left, draw an increasing branch from $(0,0)$ towards $+\infty$. On the right, draw an increasing branch from $-\infty$ to $(\pi,0)$.

spec.description: Two increasing tangent branches separated by a dashed vertical asymptote.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed sketch, including unbounded branch arrows.
